Therefore the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

(2) The membership of the women and children protection task force at the sub-district level as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements of sub-district apparatus, offices/agencies at the sub-district level, elements of the sector police (Polsek), elements of the military sub-district command (Koramil), community leaders/religious leaders, and youth elements.

3.2.rationale: The original Indonesian Article 17(2) states services must be supported by facilities including “ruang pelayanan khusus dijajaran kepolisian” (special service rooms within the police). Thus the golden label “No” appears wrong given the policy text.

3.8.evaluator_rationale: While the policy references assistance that may include clergy and mentions OPD duties in “mental and spiritual matters,” it does not explicitly establish a service unit that provides religious/spiritual counseling as a defined service.

3.8.rationale: The original Indonesian explanation of Pasal 6 huruf j explicitly lists “rohaniwan” (clergy) among forms of “pendampingan” (assistance/accompaniment) for victims, alongside psychologists/psychiatrists/advocates/family. While the regulation may not name a standalone ‘spiritual counseling unit’, it does explicitly include religious/spiritual support via clergy as part of victim assistance. This information was present in the retrieved candidates (Article 6 letter j explanation), so the judge’s ‘No’ conclusion was overly strict.

5.2.evaluator_rationale: While the text mentions cooperation with NGOs, government bodies, and includes references to 'clergy' as possible assistants, it does not explicitly describe stakeholder engagement or collaboration with religious organizations or religious leaders as institutions/partners.

5.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text does not clearly mandate engagement/partnership with religious organizations/leaders as stakeholders. It mentions cooperation with government levels and “lembaga non pemerintah” (non-government institutions) (Pasal 28) and networks with NGOs/universities/law enforcement (Pasal 13(2) huruf f). Religious leaders appear only as individuals in task-force membership (“tokoh masyarakat/tokoh agama” in Pasal 26(2) and Pasal 27(2)) and as possible victim assistants (“rohaniwan” in Penjelasan Pasal 6 huruf j), not as institutional religious stakeholder engagement. The retrieved passages did not include Pasal 26/27 anyway. Given the text, the predicted “No” is defensible and the golden “Yes” likely over-interprets incidental mentions of religious figures as ‘engagement’.
